questions.stem: The Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri were all instituted in 1954. Which of these ranks immediately below the Bharat Ratna in the order of precedence?

options.option_text: Padma Shri, awarded for distinguished service in any field
Padma Bhushan, awarded for distinguished service of high order
Padma Vibhushan, for exceptional and distinguished service to nation
All three Padma awards share equal precedence below Bharat Ratna

questions.explanation: The civilian honours hierarchy is: Bharat Ratna → Padma Vibhushan → Padma Bhushan → Padma Shri. Padma Vibhushan is the second highest. A common error is confusing Padma Bhushan (3rd) with Padma Vibhushan (2nd) because the latter's name is less frequently recalled.

questions.stem: India's highest sporting honour was renamed from 'Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award' to 'Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award' in which year?

options.option_text: 2019, after a sports ministry committee recommendation
2020, as a tribute during the Tokyo Olympics selection
2021, announced by Prime Minister Modi on 6 August 2021
2022, as part of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav celebrations

questions.explanation: PM Narendra Modi announced the renaming on 6 August 2021, coinciding with Major Dhyan Chand's birth anniversary. Option B is a tempting distractor because the Tokyo Olympics were held in 2021, but the announcement was on 6 August, not tied to selection; 2020 was the year the Games were originally scheduled.

questions.stem: The Vyas Samman, presented annually by the K.K. Birla Foundation, recognises outstanding literary works published in the preceding ten years in which Indian language?

options.option_text: Sanskrit, for works composed in the preceding decade
Hindi, for works published in the preceding ten years
Urdu, for works published in the preceding fifteen years
Bengali, for works published in the preceding ten years

questions.explanation: The Vyas Samman (instituted 1991) by K.K. Birla Foundation is specifically for outstanding Hindi literature published in the preceding ten years. Candidates often confuse it with the Saraswati Samman (also by K.K. Birla Foundation) which covers all 22 scheduled languages — the Saraswati Samman is the better-known prize; Vyas Samman is its Hindi-language counterpart.

questions.stem: The Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology, awarded by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), stipulates an upper age limit for eligible scientists. What is that age limit?

options.option_text: 40 years, to specifically reward early-career researchers
45 years, recognising outstanding mid-career contributions
50 years, to include both emerging and senior scientists
55 years, extended to cover senior researchers and fellows

questions.explanation: The SSB Prize (instituted 1957) requires candidates to be 45 years or younger as of 31 December of the year of the prize. It covers seven science and technology disciplines. The 40-year cutoff is a common wrong recall — that applies to some fellowship schemes, not the Bhatnagar Prize.

questions.stem: The Gandhi Peace Prize is awarded annually by the Government of India to individuals or institutions for contributions through non-violent and other Gandhian methods. In which year was it instituted?

options.option_text: 1948, following the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi
1969, to celebrate the birth centenary of Mahatma Gandhi
1995, to mark the 125th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi
2001, as a millennium peace initiative of the Vajpayee government

questions.explanation: The Gandhi Peace Prize was instituted in 1995 to commemorate Gandhi's 125th birth anniversary. Option B is the most tempting distractor because 1969 (Gandhi's centenary) is a significant milestone, but the prize was not established then. The first recipient was Julius Nyerere of Tanzania.

questions.stem: In India's wartime gallantry award system, which option lists the three highest decorations in CORRECT DESCENDING ORDER from most to least prestigious?

options.option_text: Param Vir Chakra → Vir Chakra → Maha Vir Chakra
Maha Vir Chakra → Param Vir Chakra → Vir Chakra
Param Vir Chakra → Maha Vir Chakra → Vir Chakra
Vir Chakra → Maha Vir Chakra → Param Vir Chakra

questions.explanation: The correct wartime hierarchy is: Param Vir Chakra (highest) → Maha Vir Chakra → Vir Chakra. Option A ('PVC → VC → MVC') swaps the second and third positions, which is the classic confusion. Do not conflate wartime awards with peacetime awards (Ashoka Chakra → Kirti Chakra → Shaurya Chakra), which follow a parallel but separate tier system.

questions.stem: Regarding India's peacetime gallantry awards — Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra — which statement is CORRECT?

options.option_text: Kirti Chakra outranks Shaurya Chakra; both awards can be given posthumously
Shaurya Chakra outranks Kirti Chakra; Kirti Chakra is reserved for civilians only
Ashoka Chakra and Kirti Chakra are equal in rank; Shaurya Chakra is the lowest
Kirti Chakra outranks Shaurya Chakra; only Ashoka Chakra can be given posthumously

questions.explanation: Peacetime hierarchy: Ashoka Chakra (highest) → Kirti Chakra → Shaurya Chakra. All three may be awarded posthumously — a detail many candidates miss, making option D a strong distractor. Option B reverses the Kirti/Shaurya order AND incorrectly restricts Kirti Chakra to civilians; all three are open to armed forces and civilians alike.
